bullets.title: April PCE cooler-than-expected; GDP revised down to 1.6%—macro data mixed
bullets.body: April core PCE printed 0.24% MoM vs. 0.3% consensus, holding YoY at 3.3%; headline PCE 0.4% MoM vs. 0.5% est. Q1 GDP was revised down to 1.6% from the 2.0% flash estimate. Personal income was flat MoM (vs. +0.4% est), while durable goods orders surged +7.9% vs. +4.0% expected. Jobless claims came in at 215K vs. 211K consensus.

bullets.title: Fed officials hawkish: easing bias 'no longer consistent,' inflation may not converge to target
bullets.body: St. Louis Fed Musalem said the prior easing bias is no longer consistent with risks, that policy is 'at or below' long-run neutral, and that a rate hike is possible if disinflation stalls in the next 1-2 quarters. NY Fed Williams projected near-term inflation around 4% (core ~3%) with tariff effects peaking in coming months, and emphasized anchoring inflation expectations. Both warned against relying on AI productivity gains to solve today's inflation problem.

bullets.title: US-Iran 60-day ceasefire MOU reportedly reached, pending Trump approval; oil falls, Treasuries rally
bullets.body: Axios reported U.S. and Iranian negotiators agreed to a 60-day memorandum of understanding extending the ceasefire and launching nuclear talks, including Iran removing Hormuz mines within 30 days. Trump requested a few days to review before signing off. Oil turned negative on the headline while 10-year Treasury yields fell ~2.8bps to 4.45% and the 1Y inflation swap moved back below 3%.

bullets.title: 7-year Treasury auction strong: 3rd-highest foreign demand on record, 0.1bps stop-through
bullets.body: The 7-year note cleared at 4.290% vs. WI 4.291% (0.1bps stop-through). Indirect bidder takedown surged to 78.4% from 58.4% prior, the 3rd-highest foreign demand on record. Direct bidder participation dropped sharply to 11.2% from 30.0%; bid-to-cover stable at 2.52.

bullets.title: Credit vol at 5th-percentile since 2012; Morgan Stanley recommends payer spread hedges
bullets.body: CDX realized vol continues declining; 3-month credit vols in 5th percentile since 2012 outright and near all-time lows relative to equity vol. MS notes credit market is pricing near perfection on Iran, with normalized credit vol skew in 92nd percentile. Recommends payer spread and ratio payer spread hedges to protect against geopolitical-driven selloff at low premium cost.

bullets.title: S&P 500 hits new all-time high; tech sector tracking back-to-back 10%+ monthly gains (last seen 2009)
bullets.body: The S&P 500 made a new all-time high Thursday, with the S&P 500 IT Index +1.3% and software sector +3.5% led by SaaS/data names. The tech sector is on pace for consecutive 10%+ monthly gains, a frequency last seen in March-April 2009 post-financial crisis. VIX broke below 16 intraday. Gamma squeeze dynamics and Iran ceasefire optimism supported the tape.

bullets.title: Consumer finances deteriorating: savings rate at 2.6% (lowest since Apr 2008), real wages negative, credit card delinquencies at 13.1% (highest since 2011)
bullets.body: The US personal savings rate dropped to 2.6%, well below the 30-year average of 5.7% and lowest since April 2008, as personal spending outpaces flat income growth. Real wage growth has turned negative. Credit card balances 90+ days delinquent hit 13.1%, the highest since 2011, signaling broad consumer financial stress.

bullets.title: Anthropic raises $65B Series H at $965B valuation; Amazon commits $5B
bullets.body: Anthropic closed a $65B Series H round at $965B post-money valuation, co-led by Capital Group, Coatue, D1, GIC, ICONIQ, and XN. Amazon committed $5B as part of $15B in hyperscaler participation. Strategic infrastructure partners include Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix. Anthropic simultaneously launched Claude Opus 4.8 with unchanged standard pricing ($5/$25 per million tokens) and a new Fast Mode tier ($10/$50 per million tokens).

bullets.title: DELL surges 30%+ AH on massive AI server beat: FY27 revenue guidance raised 18% to $167B, AI server guide raised to $60B
bullets.body: Dell Q1 revenue of $43.84B beat consensus $35.74B by 23%; EPS $4.86 vs. $2.96 est. (64% beat). ISG revenue $29B (+181% YoY) vs. $22.4B consensus; AI-optimized server revenue $16.1B (+757% YoY). FY27 guidance raised to $165-169B (from $138-142B), AI server revenue raised to ~$60B (+144% YoY from prior ~$50B), and EPS raised to $17.90 vs. prior $12.90. Supply constraints (DRAM, NAND, CPUs) cited as the only limiter—not demand.

bullets.title: EPC labor—not grid access—is the binding constraint on data center and power buildout
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley/GE Vernova research finds EPC construction execution is 'the gating item' for data center and power generation project completion. NextEra notes viable EPC contractors have shrunk from 9-11 to just 4. Sterling rallied 50% on 1Q with 80% YoY backlog growth; Argan's backlog grew from ~$800M to nearly $3B with stock up ~1,300%. HUT, WULF, and IREN all highlight EPC execution certainty as a competitive edge.

bullets.title: Snowflake $6B AWS deal and AI consumption acceleration catalyst for broader software re-rating
bullets.body: Snowflake committed $6B over five years to AWS Graviton CPUs and reported product revenue beat of ~5% with raised FY27 outlook, driving the stock +36% on AI data consumption (Cortex Code) acceleration. Analysts including Dan Ives see the AWS tie-up as a game-changer and a major positive for the broader software AI monetization narrative; SNOW product revenue/CRPO growth accelerating to mid-30s.

bullets.title: NVIDIA pushing InP laser capacity 20x by 2030; supply chain agreed to 12x—optical bottleneck forming
bullets.body: Rosenblatt checks indicate NVIDIA requested InP laser capacity to scale 20x from 2025 to 2030 for CPO deployments; supply chain vendors committed to 12x as a compromise. The gap signals a potential structural optical component supply constraint as AI rack density scales toward megawatt levels.

bullets.title: Micron EVP: meaningful memory supply only arrives late 2027; HBM4 thermal challenges create new materials demand
bullets.body: Micron's EVP and Chief Business Officer said meaningful memory chip supply will only start coming online in late 2027, with ramp in 2028, supporting pricing power. SK hynix HBM4 faces significant heat dissipation issues, creating demand for in-chip thermal conductive filler materials priced at ~RMB 6M per ton by Japanese suppliers.

bullets.title: Fed's neutral rate debate: rising yields reflect higher r*, not recession; UBS says markets overestimate hawkishness
bullets.body: Musalem said recent Treasury yield increases mostly reflect a higher expected neutral rate and persistent inflation—not recession fears. However, UBS counters that markets are overestimating Fed hawkishness and rate hike probability, with inflation trends anchored and Fed easing expected to resume in December. The 7-year auction's surge in foreign demand supports UBS's view that the bond market remains well-bid.

bullets.title: Goldman data center power projection: 8.5% of US peak demand by 2027 (from 4.1% in 2025)
bullets.body: Goldman projects data centers will consume 8.5% of US peak power demand in 2027, more than doubling from 4.1% in 2025. Co-located generation expected to serve 22-32 GW by 2030. Data center tax credit pushback noted in Ohio and South Carolina amid economic impact reviews.

bullets.title: MDB strong beat: Q2 guide 5% above consensus, Atlas growth accelerating on AI workloads
bullets.body: MongoDB Q1 revenue $687.6M beat consensus $664.5M by $23M; Atlas revenue grew 29% YoY (vs. 26% expected); Q2 guidance midpoint $732M beat consensus by ~$30M, implying acceleration despite tougher compares. FY27 guidance raised by $60M; FCF beat by $80M; EAs grew ~20% YoY vs. ~5% expected. Citi maintains Buy with $450 PT (38% upside) citing AI-native consumption ramps.

bullets.title: Meta: Zuckerberg signals potential cloud computing market entry if excess datacenter capacity materializes
bullets.body: Meta CEO Zuckerberg said the company could enter the cloud computing market if its datacenter capacity exceeds internal needs—potentially monetizing surplus AI infrastructure investment. This positions Meta as a potential future hyperscaler competitor to AWS, Azure, and GCP.

bullets.title: Microsoft to release new coding models at Build Conference; AI chief claims 18-month timeline to automate white-collar work
bullets.body: Microsoft plans to release new homegrown coding models next week at its Build Conference to boost GitHub Copilot competitiveness. Separately, Microsoft's AI chief stated a goal of automating all white-collar work within 18 months—a signal of the pace of AI deployment across the enterprise.

bullets.title: AAII bullish sentiment below historical average second straight week; retail participation declining
bullets.body: AAII bullish sentiment bounced back for the week ending May 27 but remains below the 37.5% historical average for a second consecutive week. Separately, industry data shows retail trading volumes declining, with retail equity volume correlating closely with S&P 500 movements—a potential headwind to momentum breadth.

bullets.title: ECB June rate hike setup confirmed; April minutes show no dovish pushback, baseline includes two hikes
bullets.body: ECB April 29-30 meeting minutes show no substantive pushback from hawks; June explicitly set as the appropriate time to hike given new Iran conflict data. ECB baseline scenarios incorporate two rate hikes with inflation marginally above 2% medium-term; the situation trending toward adverse scenario suggests more than one hike may be warranted.
